narrative:
The 2023 Milwaukee Brewers opened the season with a burst of energy that announced their intentions to the NL Central. An 18-9 April — powered by early fireworks from Garrett Mitchell and a clutch Brice Turang single that plated multiple runs — established the Brewers as one of baseball's most dangerous teams. Their pitching staff, anchored by a 3.71 ERA, was already showing the miserly efficiency that would define their year.

May brought turbulence. At 11-16, the Brewers stumbled through a brutal stretch that exposed cracks in the bullpen, with Peter Strzelecki surrendering back-breaking home runs and the offense going quiet at critical moments. June and July were similarly uneven — Matt Bush's inability to hold leads and Elvis Peguero getting torched by Ozzie Albies' three-run blast kept the Brewers from pulling away in the division. Yet the team kept grinding; Jahmai Jones' clutch double in early July and Joey Wiemer's go-ahead single in June showed this was a roster with resolve even when the big clips told a darker story.

August and September saw the Brewers catch fire, going 17-9 and 17-11 respectively to lock up 92 wins and the NL Central title. Brice Turang emerged as a clutch performer, Mark Canha delivered timely hits, and even the defense contributed — a pivotal error gifted the Brewers a critical run in August. Andrew Chafin's late-season struggles and Rowdy Tellez's double-play sting in September were blips in an otherwise dominant final stretch that had Milwaukee entering October with genuine momentum.

The Wild Card round against the Arizona Diamondbacks proved to be a harsh ending. Corbin Burnes, the ace, was touched for home runs by Corbin Carroll and Gabriel Moreno in Game 1, and double plays at the worst moments stifled Milwaukee's offense. Tyrone Taylor's solo blast offered a brief spark, but the Brewers couldn't sustain pressure against a hot Arizona team. Freddy Peralta was carved up in Game 2 as Carroll and Ketel Marte did the damage. A 92-win season, built on grit and pitching, was ended in the shortest postseason format — a bittersweet conclusion to one of Milwaukee's better recent campaigns.

chapters.title: Fast Out of the Gate
chapters.description: An 18-9 April powered by Mitchell's pop and Turang's clutch hitting announced the Brewers as NL Central contenders.

chapters.title: May Stumble
chapters.description: A brutal 11-16 May exposed bullpen vulnerabilities as Strzelecki surrendered multiple crushing home runs.

chapters.title: Grinding Through Summer
chapters.description: Milwaukee posted winning records in June and July despite high-leverage bullpen blowups, relying on clutch hits from unlikely heroes to stay afloat.

chapters.title: August–September Surge
chapters.description: Back-to-back winning months of 17-9 and 17-11 cemented the division title as Turang, Canha, and the defense rose to the moment.

chapters.title: October Ends Too Soon
chapters.description: The Wild Card round against Arizona became a story of double plays and home runs surrendered, as the Brewers' promising season was cut short in two games.
